clue.text: Is it possible invalid almost should get a tube?

parts.note: 'can' asks whether something is possible, as in 'can it be done?'

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: null, as in 'null and void', means having no legal force
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether a nearly useless item should be fitted with a tube.
explanation.walkthrough: Medically a cannula is the thin tube slipped into a vein or body cavity.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannula is a thin flexible tube inserted into the body for drainage or drug delivery.

clue.text: Part of machine getting computer science absorbed — which makes it think?

parts.note: a cog is a toothed wheel in a machine
IT, information technology, stands loosely for computing
ate means consumed or absorbed

explanation.surface: A machine part takes in some computing and starts to think.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests artificial intelligence; 'absorbed' is past tense eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To cogitate is to ponder or reflect deeply, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Being nosey, see rocket launcher at Canaveral's base

parts.note: NASA, the US space agency, launches its rockets from Cape Canaveral in Florida

indicators.note: the base of a word in a down clue is its bottom, final letter

parts.note: the word Canaveral ends in L, the apostrophe-s being only the possessive

explanation.surface: Someone prying watches a space rocket go up at the Florida launch site.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is ignored for the base letter; it ends the word Canaveral.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose, which 'nosey' in its literal sense covers.

clue.text: This country gets bad weather by end of June? No — it's somewhere else

parts.note: for a British setter, this country is the UK
rain is the bad weather

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the word June ends in E

explanation.surface: Britain gets rain at the end of June, but the clue insists the place is elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay seems to describe Britain itself, so the definition has to say the answer is a different country.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is an eastern European nation, so it is a place other than Britain.

clue.text: I said, parts damaged in this plant

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words are used as written
the letters of this word are used as written

explanation.surface: Someone reports that bits of this plant were damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy leafy houseplant, famous in Victorian parlours.

clue.text: Praised criminal in state of hopelessness

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters of the neighbouring word are twisted

parts.note: the letters of this word are used as written

explanation.surface: Someone praised turns out to be a criminal and falls into hopelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the condition of having lost all hope, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Completely useless English fellow

parts.note: a dud is something that fails entirely

explanation.surface: A man from England who is utterly hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Dude is an informal word for a man or guy.

clue.text: Blow! This chap gets silk, initially, as bandages!

parts.note: a swat is a sharp blow
he is a pronoun for a man

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word

parts.note: the word silk begins with S

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims as a man wraps wounds in silk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow!' reads as a mild curse; it is a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Swathes are strips of cloth wrapped around something, a bandage sense of the word.

clue.text: Headless rodent spotted by mother somewhere in Europe

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a hamster is a small rodent
a dam is the mother of an animal, especially livestock

explanation.surface: A decapitated rodent noticed by its mother somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the capital of the Netherlands, a European city.

clue.text: Fat cigarette discovered in jacket

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cannabis joint, a hand-rolled cigarette
second meaning: a ... jacket, a thick double-breasted coat

explanation.surface: A joint found in a coat pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Reefer is slang for a cannabis cigarette and also the name of a short heavy sailor's coat.

clue.text: Snail perhaps, found in Gourmet food establishment with glamping accommodation?

parts.note: a gastro is short for a gastropub, a pub serving high-quality food
glamping sites often offer pods, small wooden shelters, to sleep in

explanation.surface: A snail turning up in an upmarket pub that also offers luxury camping.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails belong to the gastropods, the mollusc class that moves on a muscular foot; 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Place in church where, briefly, "I will" may be heard

indicators.note: something heard rather than seen points to a word that sounds like the spoken phrase

parts.note: shortened, 'I will' becomes the contraction I'll

explanation.surface: The wedding vow spoken at the spot in church where the couple stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The contraction I'll is pronounced exactly like the church walkway; the surface neatly sets the wedding scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is the passage between the pews of a church, walked by a bride.

clue.text: Agreed, part-time soldiers (fifty) gave out pork pies

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
pork pies is Cockney rhyming slang for lies, so giving them out is lying

explanation.surface: Reservist soldiers in a group of fifty told fibs, or perhaps handed out snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: A pork pie is a British cold pastry; in rhyming slang 'pork pies' means lies, and the surface pretends it is food.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures that tallied matched up or corresponded, so 'agreed' is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Revolutionary English (Home Counties) dairy product

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary in crosswords
the Home Counties around London lie in the south-east of England, SE

explanation.surface: An English dairy product from the counties around London, described as revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like praise for the product or a reversal signal; it is Che Guevara.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese is made from milk curds, which makes it a classic dairy foodstuff.

clue.text: Favours pull on spliff, inhaling: Roger's head swimming!

parts.note: backs means supports or favours

indicators.note: inhaling takes something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a toke is a drag on a joint

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the name Roger begins with R

explanation.surface: Smoking a joint leaves Roger's head swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming' looks like dizziness; it defines a swimming style.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstroke is a style of swimming done lying on one's back.

clue.text: Story involving British chart

indicators.note: a story involving something wraps around it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A narrative that includes a British diagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A table sets data out in rows and columns, so it is a kind of chart.

clue.text: Reserves hour with little person, making item of library furniture?

parts.note: to book is to reserve
an elf is a small mythical being

explanation.surface: Someone books an hour with a small person to make library furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookshelf holds books, the standard fitting in any library.

clue.text: "Bubbles" seen in TV series: first of all staging unusually dramatic scenes

parts.note: a soap is a long-running TV drama series

indicators.note: first of all means the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the four words begin S, U, D and S

explanation.surface: A soap opera stages unusually dramatic scenes featuring a character called Bubbles.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'Bubbles' make it look like a character's name in the soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapsuds are the froth of tiny bubbles made by soap in water.

clue.text: Doubly a fool, taking in killer

indicators.note: doubly says the fool is given two times over, side by side

parts.note: an ass is a fool
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone twice over a fool for letting a murderer into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubly' makes the fool appear twice, and 'taking' simply attaches the word in to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, typically one who kills a prominent person for political motives.

clue.text: 25 quid given to Star's companion for a ride?

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds sterling
Trek is the word that partners Star in Star Trek

explanation.surface: Twenty-five pounds handed to a celebrity's sidekick so they can go on a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: Quid is British slang for a pound; 'Star' looks like a celebrity but is the first half of the TV title.
explanation.definitionFit: A pony trek is an outing on horseback across country, which is a kind of ride.

clue.text: Stir fry snot? That's pants!

indicators.note: to stir is to mix up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words are used as written

explanation.surface: A disgusting cooking instruction dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is British slang for rubbish, which fits the exclamation; it is also the underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are men's briefs, a type of pants in British usage meaning underwear.

clue.text: Parade mostly includes such marches

indicators.note: the phrase includes the letters, which sit inside it across the two words

parts.note: the letters sit across the end of Parade and the start of mostly

explanation.surface: A parade mostly consists of such marches.
explanation.definitionFit: Demos is short for demonstrations, protest marches by crowds.

clue.text: Bases storing last of weapons for tyrannical leaders

indicators.note: something storing another keeps it inside

parts.note: depots are bases for storing supplies

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the word weapons ends in S

explanation.surface: Military bases holding weapons for dictators.
explanation.definitionFit: Despots are rulers with absolute and often cruel power.

clue.text: Maiden with incense as Nativity prop

parts.note: to incense is to anger, the verb sense, not the fragrant smoke

explanation.surface: A young woman bearing incense in a Nativity play.
explanation.walkthrough: M for maiden is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over. Incense looks like the Magi's gift; read as a verb, it means anger.
explanation.definitionFit: The manger is the feeding trough used as the baby's crib in Nativity scenes.

clue.text: Guarantee finding animal by river

parts.note: an ass, or donkey, is the animal here
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A promise of finding a beast beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To assure someone is to promise them confidently, so it is a verb synonym of guarantee.

clue.text: Stares excitedly, restraining energy, as piece of mosaic revealed

indicators.note: restraining something holds it in, so one piece sits inside the other
doing something excitedly is agitated, so the letters of the word are stirred up

parts.note: the letters of this word are used as written

explanation.surface: Someone gazes eagerly as a fragment of mosaic is uncovered.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small tiles of glass or stone that make up a mosaic.

clue.text: Ecstasy — diet version — for the chosen ones?

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
lite labels low-calorie diet versions of foods

explanation.surface: A low-calorie version of a party drug for a select few.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the select group regarded as the best.

clue.text: Technical details written up to obtain mushrooms

indicators.note: written up in a down answer means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a spec is a technical specification

explanation.surface: Getting specifications recorded to acquire some fungi.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceps are porcini, prized edible wild fungi.

clue.text: Gather leader of aborigines found in valley

indicators.note: a thing found in a place lies inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word aborigines begins with A

explanation.surface: A tribal leader rallies people in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather bit by bit, originally collecting leftover grain after harvest.

clue.text: Savings — from earnings, initially — come in so erratically

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the word earnings begins with E

indicators.note: erratic means irregular, so the letters arrive in no fixed order

parts.note: the letters of these words are used as written

explanation.surface: Money put aside out of wages comes in on an irregular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Economies are cutbacks in spending, so they are savings made.

clue.text: Declines to accept official applications

parts.note: a ref, or referee, is the official in a game
uses are applications, as in practical ways of applying something

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat turns down requests made on forms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Applications' suggests forms to fill in; here it means practical uses.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse something is to turn it down rather than take it.

clue.text: Oriental holiday at beginning of November

parts.note: Easter is a public holiday in spring

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word November begins with N

explanation.surface: An Asian festival falling at the start of November.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and eastern both describe things from the East, so they are synonyms.
